Every entry is PARAPHRASED in Sami's own words -- never verbatim, no quotes, no copied source text, no source links/credits. Schema per item: { title, summary (paraphrased prose), type: "news" | "rumor", date (YYYY-MM-DD), source (optional short label, e.g. a publication NAME for context -- NOT a link), game (optional tag), probability (rumors only: integer 0-100 = how likely it is true) }. HOW SAMI ADDS ITEMS: paste a new object into this "items" array. Use type "news" for confirmed/reported happenings and type "rumor" for unconfirmed leaks/speculation; rumors should include a probability (0-100). Newest first is nice but the page does not require it. These seed entries are GENERIC placeholders -- replace them with real ones. Later the creator's research/truth pipeline can auto-generate and write items here.

items.title: Big open-world RPG gets a major performance patch
items.summary: The team behind one of last year's headline open-world RPGs has pushed a sizable update that mostly targets how the game runs. From what is being reported, frame pacing on consoles is noticeably smoother and a long-standing stutter when loading new areas has finally been addressed. There are also some quieter quality-of-life tweaks to the inventory and map screens. Nothing about the story changes, but for anyone who bounced off it because of the rough performance, it sounds like a good moment to jump back in.

items.title: Long-awaited co-op shooter slips to early next year
items.summary: A co-op shooter that a lot of people had pencilled in for this fall is now aiming for early next year instead. The studio framed the delay as wanting more time to polish the higher difficulty modes and stamp out matchmaking issues that showed up in testing. Disappointing if you were counting on it for the holidays, but a few extra months to land it properly is usually the better outcome. Expect a fresh gameplay look closer to the new window.

items.title: Indie hit adds a free hard mode after community requests
items.summary: One of this year's surprise indie successes just dropped a free update built almost entirely around player feedback. The headline addition is a tougher difficulty tier for people who felt the base game was too gentle once they learned the systems. There are also a handful of new accessibility options going the other direction, so the update widens the audience on both ends. It is a small team, and the fact that they keep shipping meaningful free content is doing a lot for their reputation.

items.title: Sequel to a beloved single-player action game rumored for a year-end reveal
items.summary: A sequel to a beloved single-player action game is supposedly already deep in development, with an announcement expected before the end of the year. Multiple loosely connected hints point the same direction, but nothing official has confirmed it, so treat it as a strong maybe rather than a sure thing.

items.title: Popular console exclusive maybe heading to PC next year
items.summary: Talk is circulating that a popular console exclusive could finally come to PC sometime next year. The chatter is consistent, yet it leans heavily on storefront listings that can easily be placeholders, so treat it as plausible rather than settled.

items.title: Older trilogy remaster collection rumored, but already denied once
items.summary: There is a persistent claim that a major studio is quietly working on a remaster collection of an older trilogy. It keeps resurfacing, but it has been denied once already and the supposed timing keeps shifting, which makes it hard to take at face value.
